by an electric field.
Which type of radiation is being emitted?
Which statement about two nuclei that are isotopes of the same element is correct?

options.A: The nuclei each have the same acceleration when in the same uniform electric field.
options.B: The nuclei each have the same number of neutrons.
options.C: The nuclei each have the same number of nucleons.
options.D: Uncharged atoms containing the nuclei each have the same number of electrons.

stem:
When α-particles are fired at a thin metal foil, most of the particles pass straight through but a few
are deflected by a large angle.
Which change would increase the proportion of α-particles deflected by a large angle?

options.A: using α-particles with greater kinetic energy
options.C: using a foil made of a metal with fewer protons in its nuclei
options.D: using a source emitting more α-particles per unit time

energies?

stem:
A nucleus of a radioactive element emits an α-particle, then a β⁻ particle and then another
β⁻ particle.
Which statement describes the final element that is produced?

options.A: It is a different element of higher proton number than the original element.
options.B: It is a different element of lower nucleon number than the original element.
options.C: It is an isotope of the original element.
options.D: It is the same element as the original element but with a different proton number.

stem:
In an experiment on α-particle scattering, α-particles are directed at a thin gold foil. Most of the
α-particles pass straight through the foil or are deflected by a small angle. A small number of
α-particles are deflected by a large angle.
Which statement cannot be deduced from this experiment?

options.B: Most of the mass of an atom is concentrated in the nucleus.
options.C: The nucleus of an atom contains protons.
options.D: The nucleus of an atom is small compared to the size of an atom.
